answers.answer: AMAT stays strengthening. The threat's own stated basis is CXMT HBM3E trial production, one generation behind HBM4, mass production not before 2027, with no volume or yield disclosed. That is a memory-supplier price/share threat (MU, SKHY). It reaches AMAT only second-order: (i) a CXMT-driven memory price decline cutting DRAM capex at MU/SKHY/Samsung, which needs a within-basis ASP decline that the tracker does not show (HBM3E has no within-basis trend; cross-basis change is meaningless), or (ii) export-control retaliation, which is the separate 09-24 summit item and is already in evidence_against. Exposure figures: China was 28% of Q3 FY26 revenue vs 35% a year earlier, and DRAM revenue including HBM packaging was +52% y/y at a record; the reported quarter and the Q4 guide of $10.25B were both above the Street. Higher memory capacity anywhere is tool demand, not a cut to it. I do not treat the TRIM trigger as thesis evidence. The verdict would change on a within-basis HBM3E/DRAM contract decline or a tightening of SME controls at the summit.
